previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including chronic pancreatitis, iron deficiency anemia, depression, and lipodermatosclerosis was admitted for a one-week history of odynophagia, nausea, vomiting, and poor oral intake. Initial evaluation showed no evidence of obstruction, pancreatitis, or infection. An EGD revealed mild Z-line irregularity and antral gastritis, with biopsies taken for further analysis. A barium esophagram showed a small hiatal hernia and markedly increased small bowel transit time, explaining her episode of postprandial diarrhea. Her swallowing pain improved with IV PPI and supportive care, and she advanced to a regular diet. She was discharged home on her baseline medications with instructions to follow up with gastroenterology for biopsy results and ongoing management of rapid intestinal transit and gastritis.
